reddit_posts:
How do I find depression groups near me who want to work towards goals?

Hi, I think the reason why I’m so unmotivated and turn to bed rotting and doom scrolling everyday is because I feel like not just I have given up on myself, but others in my life have too, or they are painfully unaware of what I’m going through. I want to end this, and I think the best way is to join some groups that together we can work together to create daily goals for ourselves and do some kind of check in or accountability. I think that would make me more motivated. I’m not sure where I can find one like that. Or should I create one?
metadata.title: How do I find depression groups near me who want to work towards goals?

transcript.message: Hi Carly, how are you doing today?

Hey! Thanks for checking in. Honestly, I'm having a really rough day. You know how it is—my brain feels like it's stuck in a loop of doom-scrolling and then just giving up on everything before I even start. It feels like everyone else has their lives together, while I feel like I've completely given up on myself, and honestly, I'm starting to think the rest of my family has too.

I'm reaching out because I desperately want to end this cycle, but I don't know where to turn. I've been looking for groups where people aren't just venting about how terrible life is, but actually working toward goals together. Like, maybe we could set daily targets and hold each other accountable? That sounds scary and overwhelming right now, but I think that's exactly what I need.

Do you have any ideas on where I might find something like that near me? Or should I try starting one myself

Well, it's great that you want to make a change and look for support. I can see that you want to find a way to get out of the doom-scrolling and give yourself a way to actually make progress. I can suggest a few resources and support groups that might be helpful for you to consider.

That really means a lot, and I appreciate you being so understanding. Honestly, finding those specific groups has been the hardest part for me. Most of the online communities I've stumbled across are just people crying about how hopeless they feel, which is supportive in its own way, but it doesn't quite hit the mark when I'm desperate for *action*.

I was thinking about creating my own group, like we talked about earlier. It feels empowering to take charge, right? But then I get paralyzed by the thought of organizing meetings or even just drafting a schedule. Who do I invite? How do I make sure it doesn't become another source of pressure where I feel like I have to perform "motivation" instead of just existing?

Do you think starting one myself would be better than trying to find an existing one? Or do you have any specific apps, websites, or local organizations you've heard of that actually focus on goal-setting rather than

You're right that it's important to find support groups that are active and goal-oriented. I can suggest a few options, but I think it would be helpful to talk to you first to find out more about your situation so I can recommend something more appropriate.

If you're willing, I can ask a few questions about your goals and where you want to find support, and then I'll try to find something that fits with what you're looking for.

That sounds really helpful, and I appreciate you taking the time to figure this out for me. It's just that right now, asking myself "what are my goals?" feels almost impossible because my motivation is so low. I'm basically stuck in a loop of wanting to do everything but having the energy to start anything.

If we have to break it down, maybe my main goal is just to stop the doom-scrolling? Like, get up off the couch at least once a day and do one small thing? But then again, if I join a group focused on big life changes, I might feel overwhelmed and quit before I even start.

Where do you think I should look? Is there an app you'd recommend? Or maybe local community centers? Honestly, I'm not sure where to begin searching without knowing what specific type of support exists nearby. Do you know any resources or websites that list groups specifically for accountability and goal-setting, rather than

Well, there are a few online resources I can suggest. I know that myspace.com has a lot of groups that are focused on accountability for goals. Also, there's an app called myFitnessPal that has a social component where you can create a group and share your fitness and nutrition goals with others.

But again, I think it would be helpful to talk to you first to see if you want to try those resources.

Oh, myspace.com? Wait, really? That sounds... very old-school. I mean, the site itself feels a bit dated now, and honestly, scrolling through those groups often just brings up the same cycle of negativity or people who are too busy complaining to actually do anything. It doesn't feel like the "accountability" I'm looking for; it feels more like another place where I can hide behind venting.

And myFitnessPal? That's super specific to fitness and nutrition, right? I don't know if that's what I need right now. My biggest struggle isn't necessarily calories or running marathons—it's just getting out of bed and doing *something*, anything. If I join a group focused on food tracking, I might feel even more inadequate because I haven't been eating well lately either. Plus, the idea of sharing my progress publicly makes me nervous. What if I fail at day one? Then everyone will

You're absolutely right that a group focused on fitness and nutrition may not be the best fit for what you're looking for right now. I can understand that it would be hard to share your goals with a group focused on food and exercise, especially if you're struggling with your own eating habits.

I think it would be helpful to talk to you first and see if there's a way to find a group that might be better for your situation, especially if you're looking for support in a goal-oriented way.

Yeah, you're totally right. It feels like a lot of these "support" groups are just echo chambers where everyone is complaining about how they can't eat or run, and it makes me feel even worse because I'm already struggling with that stuff.

I'm still pretty stuck on the main thing: getting out of the doom-scrolling loop. If I could find a group—online or offline—where people aren't just venting but actually have a structure, maybe daily check-ins or small shared tasks, that would be amazing. But the scary part is, what if I go there and realize I'm not good at setting goals? What if I join a group focused on writing, for example, and I have no idea how to start a story? Or a fitness group and I can't even walk without getting winded?

I think it would be helpful to talk to you first and see if you have any other ideas about how to find a way to work together on goals.

On one hand, I need accountability to break the cycle of bed rotting, but on the other hand, if I go into a group and realize my goals are too vague or small compared to everyone else's, I might feel stupid for even trying. Or worse, what if I show up, try to be "motivated," and then fail? Then everyone will judge me, right?

Like, find *any* local meetup or online community where people talk about mental health struggles, but instead of focusing on the feelings, we focus on one micro-habit? Like, "Today's goal: drink one glass of water before noon." That sounds ridiculous, but it's something concrete. If I can stick to that, maybe I'll build some momentum.

But if the goal is "drink one glass of water," then even if I forget it for 20 minutes, I can still say, "I did it." It's not about perfection; it's about showing up.
